What is bright-room?

bright-room is a GitHub Organization focused on product development, knowledge sharing, and community activities through open source. Like a "bright room," we aim to be a welcoming space where anyone can find inspiration.
Open Source
All projects are published as OSS. Anyone can access the code, learn from it, and contribute.
Community Driven
Members from diverse backgrounds participate and leverage each other's strengths in development.
Practical Products
We ship real-world tools and libraries, not just learning exercises.

Contribution Guide
Contributing to bright-room is easy in 4 steps. Perfect for your first OSS contribution.
Fork the Repo
Fork the repository you want to contribute to and clone it locally.
Create a Branch
Use format like feature/xxx or fix/xxx to describe your changes.
Make Changes
Develop following coding conventions, add tests and run them.
Submit a PR
Create a Pull Request describing your changes. It will be reviewed and merged.
Coding Conventions & Rules
Follow Conventional Commits format for commit messages (feat:, fix:, docs:, etc.)
Include a summary and related Issue number in your PR description
Add tests for new features and ensure existing tests pass
Follow ESLint / Prettier config in each repository
Discuss large changes in Issues or Discussions beforehand
Frequently Asked Questions
Common questions from those considering joining.
Can beginners participate?
Absolutely! bright-room welcomes all experience levels. We value non-code contributions like documentation fixes and issue reports too. Feel free to ask questions on Discord.
How active do I need to be?
Each member contributes at their own pace. Weekends only, a few times a month — whatever works for you. There are no mandatory quotas or obligations.
Are specific languages or frameworks required?
It varies by project, but we mainly use TypeScript, React, Go, and Rust. We actively explore new technologies, so you can propose projects to learn something new.
How do you communicate?
Primarily through Discord and GitHub Issues, PRs, and Discussions. Communication is mostly asynchronous, so timezone differences aren't a concern.
Can I propose my own project ideas?
Absolutely! Share them in GitHub Discussions or the #ideas channel on Discord. Get feedback from members and launch it as a new Organization repository.
